summary: This article explains how tiny smell receptors inside your nose catch floating molecules, send signals to the brain, team up with taste, and why some smells suddenly bring back old memories.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “How Your Nose Smells the World” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a tiny part of the body that catches a certain thing and sends a signal
a tiny bit of matter too small to see, made of even smaller parts
to notice or find something, often using one of the senses

challengeTerms.def: related to the sense of smell
a rounded part shaped like a bulb; in the brain, the area that first processes smell signals
to bring a feeling, memory, or image suddenly to mind

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that smell is the sense most closely linked to memory? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how smell and taste combine to create flavor, and describe one way smell connects to memory or emotion.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review receptor, molecule, and detect, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses olfactory, bulb, and evoke to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
